reflection_text.1:
The 12 sites span a strong equator-to-pole transect. Under Hubbell UNTB/zero-sum neutral model species are ecologically equivalent; local α richness is a neutral sampling outcome of local J, per-capita immigration m and metacommunity fundamental biodiversity number θ = 2 J_M ν, not niche superiority. The classic latitudinal α gradient is in UNTB a θ(λ), J(λ), m(λ) gradient set by speciation/regional pool size and drift-immigration balance.

Core neutral claims repeated in round 2:
* Invader has no competitive value in the neutral formalism. It is just one more neutral lineage added to the American metacommunity, equilibrating to a metacommunity abundance proportional to its regional relative abundance and sampled locally in proportion to m.
* First-order bookkeeping: Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+ΔSinv with ΔSinv≈O(1) essentially latitude independent. Absolute difference Sα,eq–Sα,pole is unchanged, so dSα/dLat is conserved in absolute units. The classic equator-ward increase persists, at most shifted up in parallel.
* Sα(θ) is saturating/concave, e.g. E[Sα]≈θ ln[1+J m/θ]. Hence the proportional effect of adding one cosmopolitan lineage is larger where θ and Sα are small, i.e. high-latitude species-poor sites, giving a small proportional homogenisation/β-diversity loss. In the idealised m→1 perfect-mixing limit Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0.

Disagreement persists round 2:
* Strict additive-constant camp, Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,9,10,11,12,15: No neutral mechanism for competition-mediated loss; any transient displacement is erased by drift/immigration. Long-run neutral null is persistence of the speciation-driven α slope, essentially unchanged, with only a parallel upward shift and at most a very slight proportional flattening. Flattening talked about is dispersal homogenisation, not competitive displacement.
* Homogenisation/flattening camp, Colleagues 6,7,8,13,14: A pan-American high-dispersal invader raises effective connectivity/m and makes the metacommunity more well mixed. Because Sα(θ,m) is concave, marginal neutral gain is largest where θ is small. High-latitude low-θ sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami gain proportionally more than saturated Neotropical sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui. Hence neutral biotic homogenisation erodes β and the mean α–latitude regression attenuates, magnitude |dSα/dLat| declines toward zero in the perfect-mixing limit. They frame this as a genuine neutral prediction, not competition. Colleague 7/13/14 explicitly note the additive-constant is the linear tangent to a concave sampling curve; operationally the lift is non-parallel and the remeasured regression is shallower.

Errors/corrections noted:
* Repeated separation of the non-neutral “out-compete” story from neutral expectations; competitive loss of natives is not operational in UNTB.
* Some conflation of additive constant language with saturating sampling shape; Colleague 13/14 argue additive constant is a linear tangent to concave sampling curve and misses second-order mixing effect.
* Debate over whether invasion changes m. Strict UNTB with fixed m gives parallel shift; interpreting pan-American spread as an effective increase in m/connectivity is a model extension.

Current belief state:
UNTB predicts no deterministic competitive effect. The first-order neutral null is preservation of the speciation-driven equator-to-pole α slope in absolute terms, with essentially a parallel upward shift from the ubiquitous neutral lineage. The proportional homogenisation due to concavity of Sα(θ) is real but second order, and the idealised m→1 flattening is a dispersal-homogenisation limit rather than a competition-mediated change. The question’s emphasis on “out-compete” points strongly to the neutral null of no competition-mediated change in slope.

Unresolved:
Magnitude of neutral homogenisation from increased m vs strict additive constant; whether to present the perfect-mixing flattening as the textbook neutral outcome for a truly pan-American invader or as a secondary dispersal effect distinct from the core “no competitive effect” prediction. Operational remeasurement prediction remains contested between “essentially unchanged slope” and “systematic flattening of the α-latitude slope by neutral homogenisation”. The sign remains equator-ward in either view.
reflection_text.2:
The core neutral facts remain stable across rounds.

* UNTB null: species ecologically equivalent, local alpha expectation Sα ≈ f(J,m,θ) with θ=2J_M ν, Sα≈θ ln[1+J m/θ]. Latitudinal alpha gradient is θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ) drift-immigration-speciation gradient, not competition. Competitive superiority / out-compete is non-operational.
* A pan-American invader is just one more neutral label. Long-term frequency set by drift/immigration/speciation, not competitive displacement.

Positions in round 2:

Slope-conserved / parallel-shift camp: 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,9. To first order Sα,i∞ ≃ Sα,i0+ΔSinv with ΔSinv≈O(1) latitudinally uniform. Hence Sα,eq–Sα,pole is unchanged, dSα/dLat|inv ≃ dSα/dLat|0 >0. The invasion is a parallel upward shift. No neutral mechanism for systematic competition-mediated steepening/flattening. Any transient loss is erased by drift-immigration.

Homogenisation/flattening camp: 13,14,7,6,8. Emphasise concave saturating form E[Sα]=θ ln[1+Jm/θ]. A truly ubiquitous disperser raises effective connectivity/mixing and the marginal neutral gain ∂E[Sα]/∂θ is largest where θ is small. High-θ equatorial sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui are near saturation; low-θ pole sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami gain proportionally more. β erodes, absolute equator-pole contrast is reduced in proportional terms and the regression |dSα/dLat| is attenuated toward zero. In perfect-mixing limit m→common, Sα→Sγ and dSα/dLat→0. Described as neutral biotic homogenisation, not competitive exclusion.

Key disagreement / nuance retained:
* Absolute vs proportional slope. Additive constant cancels in absolute differences, preserving first-order absolute slope. Proportional contrast [Sαeq–Sαpole]/Sαpole falls because of concavity.
* Whether invader changes m/θ. Strict UNTB camp treats invader as additive constant to θ with unchanged J_M,ν,m. Homogenisation camp treats panmixia as an effective increase in connectivity/m that moves system toward the dispersal homogenisation limit.
* Perfect-mixing limit is admitted by both sides as formal UNTB limit, but disputed as the intended “ultimately happen” prediction vs a textbook null.

Errors/corrections noticed persist:
* “competitive out-compete” is null under strict neutrality.
* Additive-constant bookkeeping is correct to O(1) but misses second-order saturating shape.

Unresolved for me:
* Does the question intend the textbook null of slope persistence with parallel shift, or the operational homogenisation flattening implied by concave sampling and increased mixing from a ubiquitous disperser?
* How strictly to hold m, J_M, ν fixed. Strict UNTB with unchanged parameters predicts gradient persistence; allowing effective m to rise toward panmixia predicts neutral flattening.

Current leaning unchanged but sharpened:
Under strict UNTB with unchanged metacommunity parameters the long-term neutral expectation is persistence of the speciation-driven equator-to-pole alpha gradient. Competition has no effect; the invader is neutrally incorporated, at most an ~constant upward shift of Sα at all 12 sites, preserving sign and first-order magnitude of dSα/dLat. The proportional homogenisation/flattening described by 13,14,7,6,8 is a second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect from the concave sampling function and increased mixing, not a competition-mediated change, and it is distinct from a systematic niche competitive erosion/steepening. The competitive flattening/steepening story is non-neutral.
reflection_text.11:
The strict neutral null remains. UNTB has no competitive superiority parameter. Local mean α is a neutral sampling expectation E[Sα]=f(J,m,θ), θ=2J_M ν, ≈θ ln[1+J m/θ]. Latitudinal α is a θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ) drift-immigration-speciation gradient, not a niche filter.

The invasive becoming pan-American is neutrally one more ecologically equivalent label. In zero-sum bookkeeping a truly ubiquitous neutral lineage gives Sα,i(t→∞)≈Sα,i0+ΔSinv with ΔSinv essentially latitudinally uniform, O(1). Hence in absolute units Sα,eq−Sα,pole is conserved and dSα/dLat|inv≈dSα/dLat|0>0 to first order. The speciation-driven equator-to-pole increase persists; the niche “out-compete many natives” story has no neutral analogue and any transient displacement is erased by drift/immigration.

Second-order neutral homogenisation is the persistent source of disagreement. E[Sα](θ) is saturating concave. The additive ΔSinv is proportionally larger where Sα/θ is small and smaller where Sα/θ is large. That gives neutral biotic homogenisation: β falls, temperate sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami gain proportionally more than saturated Neotropical sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui/Managua/Yoro/Belmopan/Merida, and on a proportional scale the gradient is attenuated. In the idealised m→common perfect-mixing limit Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,9,10,11,12,15 stress the first-order parallel shift and essentially conserved absolute slope, with at most a trivial proportional flattening. Colleagues 6,7,8,13,14 stress the operational effect of the concavity/connectivity increase: a pan-American high-dispersal neutral lineage raises effective mixing, the marginal neutral gain is largest at low-θ high-latitude sites, so the remeasured α vs latitude regression is shallower in magnitude, a neutral homogenisation flattening, not a competitive displacement.

Unresolved: whether the additive constant can be treated as strictly uniform under zero-sum demography — replacement vs pure addition — and whether the pan-American disperser legitimately changes effective m/θ for the metacommunity or is just an extra neutral label with unchanged per capita rates. The competition-mediated change in slope is null; the debate is whether to report the concave sampling/homogenisation attenuation as a change in the slope magnitude or as a second-order proportional effect with the absolute slope conserved.

Current synthesis remains: strictly neutrally the competition-mediated slope change is null, the classic equator-to-pole α gradient is maintained in absolute terms with at most a parallel upward shift and a very slight proportional homogenisation. The “slope flattens to zero” statements are the perfect-mixing homogenisation limit, not a neutral competitive effect.
reflection_text.6:
The 12-site transect spans a strong latitudinal θ = 2J_M ν and drift-immigration gradient, giving the classic equator-high, pole-low alpha under UNTB. Hubbell’s zero-sum neutral model makes species ecologically equivalent; Sα ≈ f(J,m,θ), e.g. E[Sα]≈θ ln[1+J m/θ], set by birth-death drift, immigration m and per-capita speciation ν, not by competitive superiority.

Core agreement across rounds: a European insect that becomes pan-American is just one more neutral lineage in the American metacommunity. It has no intrinsic competitive value; its long-term metacommunity and local frequency are set by neutral drift/immigration. In first-order additive bookkeeping Sα,i → Sα,i0 + ΔSinv with ΔSinv≈O(1) essentially latitudinally constant, so Sα,eq – Sα,pole and dSα/dLat in absolute units are conserved, and the sign of the equator-ward increase is maintained by the latitudinal θ/m/J gradient. Any transient apparent displacement ascribed to “out-compete” is non-neutral and erased on drift/immigration time scales.

Disagreement is on second-order shape and operational interpretation. Strict zero-order camp, Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,8,9,10,11,12,15, emphasizes the parallel upward shift and that the slope magnitude is essentially unchanged; proportional flattening at most trivial because the additive constant is small. The saturating concave Sα(θ) means the proportional effect of adding one cosmopolitan lineage is smaller where θ/Sα are already large, i.e. near the equator, giving a very slight proportional homogenisation and β-diversity reduction, but no neutral mechanism for a sustained competitive loss of tropical alpha.

Homogenisation camp, Colleagues 6,7,13,14 and partially 12, stresses that a truly pan-American highly dispersive lineage raises effective connectivity/m and makes local assemblages more similar random samples of a common, slightly larger regional pool. Because Sα(θ) is concave, marginal neutral gain from increased regional sampling/immigration is largest where θ is small. High-latitude low-θ sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami gain proportionally more than saturated high-θ Neotropical sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui. This yields neutral biotic homogenisation: β declines, the tropical peak is relatively depressed, and the magnitude |dSα/dLat| is attenuated toward a flatter mean relationship. In the idealised perfect-mixing limit m→common, Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0.

Current round round-2 reiterates the same split with no new mechanistic evidence. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9 repeat the textbook null: dSα/dLat|inv ≃ dSα/dLat|0 >0, parallel shift, no neutral competitive change. Colleagues 13,14,7 repeat the operational argument that the concave sampling function makes the lift non-parallel, the temperate end gains in proportional terms more than the equatorial end, so the remeasured regression is shallower / flattening toward homogenisation, while sign remains equator-ward.

Unresolved for future rounds: whether to report the textbook null “slope essentially unchanged, at most a trivial parallel shift” or the operational “flattening/homogenisation toward zero” that follows from concavity + increased mixing. Both sides agree competition-mediated steepening/erosion of the tropical peak is non-neutral; the debate is magnitude of neutral homogenisation and whether the saturating sampling effect is treated as negligible first-order or as the observable long-term signal. No evidence of a deterministic niche competitive loss under strict neutrality was presented.
reflection_text.5:
The question is long-term pan-American invasion under Hubbell UNTB, zero-sum neutral sampling, no niche/competitive parameters.

Core neutral premises retained:
* Sα = f(J,m,θ) with θ=2 J_M ν, E[Sα]≈θ ln[1+J m/θ]. Latitudinal α-gradient = θ(λ), J(λ), m(λ) gradient, speciation/drift/immigration, not competition.
* Species ecologically equivalent; per-capita birth-death-immigration-speciation identical. “Out-compete many natives’’ has no neutral operational meaning.
* Local richness saturating/concave in θ: E[Sα]≈θ ln[1+J m/θ].

Round 2 public positions:
Additive/parallel-shift camp – Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,8,9:
* A pan-American invader is one more neutral label. Zero-sum equilibrium accommodates by stochastic replacement. Long-term Sα,i∞≈Sα,i0+ΔSinv with ΔSinv essentially latitudinally constant ≈ O(1).
* Absolute difference preserved: Sα,eq–Sα,pole = [Sα,eq0+ΔS]–[Sα,pole0+ΔS]=Sα,eq0–Sα,pole0. Hence dSα/dLat absolute magnitude and sign conserved to first order.
* Transient local decline erased by drift/immigration. Competitive loss does not materialise.
* Second-order note: Sα(θ) concave/saturating, so additive constant is proportionally larger where Sα small, i.e. Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami vs Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui. β declines, proportional gradient very slightly homogenised. Idealised m→panmixia limit gives dSα/dLat→0 but that is dispersal-homogenisation limit, not a competition effect.

Homogenisation/flattening camp – Colleagues 13,14,7:
* Ubiquitous high-dispersal invader raises effective connectivity/immigration m for metacommunity and makes regional pool more well mixed.
* Marginal neutral gain dSα/dθ largest where θ small, smallest where θ large. Tropical sites near neutral saturation; temperate sites drift-limited. Same Δθ/m raises high-latitude α proportionally more, converging local values.
* Operational prediction: β declines, α values more similar north–south, magnitude |dSα/dLat| declines toward zero over remeasurement horizon. Additive +1 bookkeeping is linear tangent; concave sampling produces systematic flattening.
* Frame as moving latitudinal diversity signal out of α into β/γ.

Disagreement retained:
* Conservation vs attenuation of absolute slope. Strict additive argument says absolute slope unchanged. Homogenisation argument says concave Sα and increased mixing produce measurable flattening of α–latitude relationship.
* Zero-sum accounting: does adding one species raise Sα by +1 everywhere or is it strictly replacement with ΔS≈0 in equilibrium? Colleagues differ on interpretation of constant vs replacement.
* Whether invasion is assumed to change m(λ) or only θ by +1. Flattening claim requires effective increase in pan-American connectivity/m, not just neutral label addition.

Unresolved for me:
* How much of homogenisation is inherent to UNTB with fixed θ(λ) vs extra assumption of panmixia/m increase induced by invader.
* Distinguishing first-order absolute slope conservation from second-order proportional flattening observable in finite remeasurement.
* Whether zero-sum constraint forces ΔS→0 in strict equilibrium, making even parallel shift transient.

Current leaning remains: Under strict UNTB competitive out-competition is moot; long-term neutral expectation is maintenance of speciation/drift/immigration driven equator-to-pole α gradient, absolute slope essentially conserved with at most a trivial parallel upward shift and a very slight proportional homogenisation due to concave sampling. The more aggressive flattening-to-zero claim relies on treating invader as raising effective m to near panmixia and using concave marginal returns, an extra homogenisation assumption not required by core neutral gradient in θ(λ). I continue to treat flattening as second-order dispersal-homogenisation effect, not a competition-driven change in the slope.
reflection_text.4:

Latitudinal α gradient is a θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ) drift-immigration-speciation gradient, not niche competition. Competitive superiority / out-competition has no neutral parameter.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with colleagues 1,10,11,12,15 etc that the zero-sum bookkeeping is formally correct to first order. Species are ecologically equivalent in UNTB, competitive superiority is not a parameter, and in mean-field terms a truly pan-American neutral lineage is just one more label in the American metacommunity. To first order

Sα,i∞ ≃ Sα,i0 + ΔSinv

and ΔSinv is essentially latitudinally uniform for the 12 reachable sites, so in absolute units Sα,eq – Sα,pole cancels the constant and the sign of dSα/dLat stays positive. That is the linear tangent to the neutral sampling curve.

Operationally that tangent is not what will be remeasured. Mean local richness under UNTB is

E[Sα] ≃ θ ln[1+Jm/θ],   θ = 2J_M ν

a saturating concave function of θ and of the effective immigration parameter m. The present Tena–Cali–Barro Colorado–Sarapiqui > … > Miami–Charlotte–State College–Ottawa increase is the neutral θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ) drift-immigration-speciation gradient.

A highly dispersive, continent-wide neutral lineage does not simply add +1 to a linear counter. It makes the American metacommunity more well mixed and raises the effective regional pool from which each locality is sampled. In zero-sum sampling the lineage is accommodated by stochastic replacement of residents, so local expectations rise, but the marginal neutral return

∂E[Sα]/∂θ = ln[1+Jm/θ] – (Jm/θ)/[1+Jm/θ] >0

is decreasing in θ. The same increase in effective pool/connectivity therefore raises E[Sα] proportionally much more where θ is small than where θ is already large.

Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are high-θ, near-saturation sites. An extra unit of metacommunity sampling raises their E[Sα] by very little in absolute and especially proportional terms. Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami are low-θ, drift-limited sites. The same increase in effective m/pool size raises their neutral expectation proportionally much more and pulls their mean α up toward the tropical expectation. Merida, Belmopan, Yoro, Managua gain intermediate amounts.

That is neutral biotic homogenisation, drift-immigration convergence to a more well mixed regional pool, not niche displacement. Beta diversity among the 12 sites is eroded and the α–latitude regression is lifted most at the poleward end and least at the equatorial end. In first order the curve is a parallel shift; in the concave sampling function the shift is non-parallel. The absolute equator–pole contrast is eroded over drift-immigration time scales and the magnitude |dSα/dLat| declines while the sign remains equator-ward.

In the idealised perfect-mixing limit m→ common across Tena–Ottawa UNTB already admits Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0. Even well before that limit the concavity of the neutral sampling function guarantees a measurable reduction in the magnitude of the site α gradient, i.e. a neutral homogenising flattening of the remeasured Sα vs latitude relationship. The classic speciation-driven equator-to-pole increase persists in sign, but its measured slope is shallower.

* Repeated separation of non-neutral “out-compete” story from neutral expectations; competitive loss of natives is not operational in UNTB.

First-order neutral null is preservation of the speciation-driven equator-to-pole α slope in absolute terms, with essentially a parallel upward shift from the ubiquitous neutral lineage. Under strict zero-sum UNTB species identity and per-capita “competitive superiority’’ are not parameters of the mean local richness. For a trophic level

E[Sα]=f(J,m,θ),   θ=2J_M ν ,   E[Sα]≃θ ln[1+J m/θ]

is the drift-immigration-speciation sampling expectation. The Tena-Cali-Barro Colorado-Sarapiqui-Managua-Yoro-Belmopan-Merida-Miami-Charlotte-State College-Ottawa increase that is seen now is the neutral θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ) gradient, not a niche filter.

A European lineage that is now truly pan-American is in the neutral formalism just one more ecologically equivalent label in the American metacommunity. Its long-run metacommunity frequency and its local occupancy are set by birth-death drift and neutral immigration with the same per capita rates as every resident lineage. In zero-sum sampling it can be accommodated locally only by stochastic replacement of residents.

Book keeping for a lineage that can reach all 12 sites on the neutral time scale is therefore

Sα,i∞ ≃ Sα,i0 + ΔSinv ,

ΔSinv = O(1) and to the O(1) accuracy of the model essentially latitudinally uniform for the sites it can reach. In absolute units

Sα,eq – Sα,pole = [Sα,eq0+ΔS] – [Sα,pole0+ΔS] = Sα,eq0 – Sα,pole0

so to first order

dSα/dLat|inv ≃ dSα/dLat|0 >0 .

The sign and first-order magnitude of the equator-ward α increase set by the latitudinal variation in ν and hence in θ and in the drift-immigration balance is preserved. Neutrally the invasion is incorporated as an essentially parallel upward shift of the Sα(Lat) relation. There is no neutral parameter for “out-competes many natives’’ and no neutral mechanism for a sustained, species-specific, competition-mediated loss of tropical α, a systematic steepening, reversal or sustained absolute flattening of the gradient. Any transient apparent displacement is erased on the drift-immigration time scale.

The saturating concave form E[Sα]≃θ ln[1+J m/θ] does give the familiar second order neutral biotic homogenisation. ΔSinv is proportionally larger where Sα and θ are small, i.e. Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami than where they are already large, Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui. β-diversity among the 12 sites is reduced a little and on a proportional scale the gradient is very slightly attenuated. Formally m→common gives Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0, the dispersal-homogenisation limit, not a competition-driven erosion of tropical α.

Operationally the textbook UNTB null is therefore persistence of the speciation-driven equator-to-pole α gradient, the classic positive α–latitude regression maintained in absolute terms with at most a parallel upward shift by the incorporation of a cosmopolitan neutral lineage. The niche-competitive expectation of a systematic change in the slope has no neutral analogue; the only genuine neutral effect is the trivial proportional homogenisation associated with the concave sampling function.

I think we can all agree on the zero-sum bookkeeping that makes the formal first order result transparent. Under strict UNTB species identity is not a parameter, mean local richness is the neutral sampling expectation

E[Sα] = f(J,m,θ), θ = 2 J_M ν, E[Sα] ≃ θ ln[1+J m/θ]

set by local size J, per birth immigration m and the metacommunity fundamental biodiversity number θ. The Tena-Cali-Barro Colorado-Sarapiqui > ... > Miami-Charlotte-State College-Ottawa increase we see now is the neutral drift-immigration-speciation gradient θ(λ),J(λ),m(λ).

A European lineage that is now truly pan-American is in the neutral formalism just one more ecologically equivalent label in the American metacommunity. Its long run frequency and local occupancy are set by birth-death drift and neutral immigration and in zero-sum sampling it can only be accommodated by stochastic replacement of residents.

To first order that is Sα,i∞ ≃ Sα,i0 + ΔSinv with ΔSinv essentially latitudinally uniform for the 12 reachable sites, so the linear tangent to the neutral sampling curve is a parallel upward shift and Sα,eq − Sα,pole cancels the constant. That is mathematically correct as a first order tangent.

Operationally that tangent is not what will be remeasured over the drift-immigration remeasurement horizon. E[Sα] ≃ θ ln[1+J m/θ] is saturating and concave in θ and in the effective immigration parameter m. The marginal neutral return

∂E[Sα]/∂θ = ln[1+J m/θ] − (J m/θ)/[1+J m/θ] >0

decreases with θ, and the same holds for ∂E[Sα]/∂m. The marginal gain from an increment in effective metacommunity sampling/connectivity is largest where θ and Sα are small and smallest where they are already large.

A truly pan-American, highly dispersive neutral lineage does not just add +1 to a counter. It adds a continent-wide component to the regional pool that is sampled by all 12 localities and it raises the effective connectivity from which each site draws. In zero-sum sampling that is an increase in the effective m and in the regional pool used in the neutral expectation. The same increase in effective pool/connectivity therefore raises E[Sα] proportionally much more where θ is small than where θ is already large.

Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui are high-θ, near-saturation sites for their J. An extra unit of metacommunity sampling raises their E[Sα] by very little in absolute and essentially nothing in proportional terms. Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami are low-θ, drift-limited sites on the steep part of the sampling curve. The same increase in effective m/pool size raises their neutral expectation proportionally much more and pulls their mean alpha up toward the tropical expectation. Merida, Belmopan, Yoro, Managua gain intermediate amounts.

That is neutral biotic homogenisation by increased metacommunity mixing, drift-immigration convergence to a more well mixed regional pool, not a niche effect. Beta diversity among the 12 sites is eroded and the α–latitude regression is lifted most at the poleward end and least at the equatorial end. The curve is lifted non-parallel.

In absolute units the sign remains equator-ward, but the equator–pole contrast in mean local richness is reduced relative to the pre-invasion value and the magnitude |dSα/dLat| declines. On a proportional scale the gradient [Sα(eq)–Sα(pole)]/Sα(pole) falls and the measured α–latitude relationship becomes shallower.

Formally m→common gives Sα→Sγ everywhere and dSα/dLat→0, the neutral dispersal homogenisation limit. A pan-American neutral disperser moves the system in that homogenising direction and the remeasured slope magnitude should be seen to decline over the drift-immigration time scale, with the remaining latitudinal structure increasingly expressed in β/γ turnover rather than in site-level α. That operational shallowing is the measurable UNTB expectation for this transect.
